extracted.intended_audience: Council on Environmental Quality, federal agencies conducting NEPA reviews, and stakeholders (electric utilities) submitting comments on NEPA GHG guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Comments and recommended rubric for CEQ's draft NEPA guidance on when and how federal agencies should consider greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and climate effects in NEPA reviews, with emphasis on electricity-sector projects. Focuses on scope, quantification thresholds, use of sector-wide context, legal sufficiency, and avoiding speculative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency discretion to determine analysis scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should use their expertise and experience to determine how and to what degree to analyze reasonably foreseeable potential direct and indirect effects of GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage agency-specific determinations rather than a one-size-fits-all mandate; balance NEPA information requirements with practical difficulties of quantifying emissions. The Draft Guidance appropriately gives agencies significant discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify GHG emissions when substantial and explain reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should quantify GHG emissions when they are substantial and provide well-reasoned explanations for their analyses and quantifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifications should be contextualized and caveated to satisfy NEPA’s information-forcing requirements and to survive judicial scrutiny; avoid highly speculative quantification when emissions are insignificant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use existing emissions estimates, including sector-wide, for context
rubrics_metrics.description: The Draft Guidance encourages agencies to use existing emissions estimates, including sector-wide estimates, to provide context for understanding the relative magnitude of a proposed action’s GHG emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sector-wide sources (e.g., EIA) are appropriate and often sufficient to satisfy NEPA objectives; agencies should be encouraged to consider all rigorous sector-wide analyses when assessing direct and indirect emissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider larger electricity-sector emissions trends
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ should ensure final guidance encourages agencies to consider the larger context of electricity sector GHG emissions where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the power sector has reduced emissions substantially and that sector trends can affect the meaning of project-specific emissions (e.g., new transmission may enable renewables integration and reduce net emissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG impacts should not drive NEPA decisions alone
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA analyses need not give greater consideration to potential effects from GHG emissions than to other potential effects on the human environment; GHG emissions and potential climate impacts alone are not the only relevant or determinative factor in NEPA analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit that GHGs are one component among many (statutory, economic, multiple-use considerations) and should not automatically push actions to an EIS or dictate agency decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance should help agencies satisfy judicial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Final guidance should help agencies comply with applicable judicial decisions concerning the sufficiency of GHG emissions assessments undertaken to comply with NEPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical approaches so agencies can produce analyses that courts will find adequate (e.g., when courts have remanded for failure to quantify reasonably foreseeable emissions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide guidance on assessing indirect and cumulative GHG impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: CEQ should provide agencies with general guidance on how to approach indirect and cumulative impacts for GHG emissions in developing NEPA analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because such assessments are fact-specific and depend on agency authority and available information, guidance should give examples and methodologies (including when to rely on sector-wide estimates) and emphasize reasonableness and proportionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rubric/threshold for when quantification or monetization is necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: Any final guidance should recognize judicial decisions that require disclosure of social costs of GHG emissions where agencies monetize benefits, and provide a rubric for identifying when quantification or monetization is necessary to avoid litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain circumstances (e.g., when economic benefits are monetized) where courts have required disclosure of social costs, and offer a structured threshold-based approach to reduce uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the 'rule of reason' and proportionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should apply the 'rule of reason' and the 'concept of proportionality' in undertaking NEPA reviews, including when determining scope of reviews, effects, alternatives, and potential mitigation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit the extent of analysis to what is reasonable relative to the action’s scale and potential impacts to avoid disproportionate burden, cost, and delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze only reasonably foreseeable effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruct agencies to explore only reasonably foreseeable effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid speculative or remote-effect analyses; do not require agencies to consider effects that are not reasonably foreseeable at the time of the NEPA review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative GHG emissions alone do not trigger an EIS
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that cumulative GHG emissions—an individual proposed action’s GHG emissions together with all others worldwide—alone do not require an environmental impact statement (EIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit that treating cumulative global GHGs as automatically significant would inappropriately send virtually every action to an EIS; avoid that anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit net environmental effects and beneficial GHG reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that some proposed actions will reduce GHG emissions directly or indirectly and so should receive positive credit in the NEPA analysis for those beneficial effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct agencies to consider net effects (e.g., a natural gas unit replacing coal reduces net emissions) and to account for benefits where relevant to the decisionmaking and scope of further analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit alternatives to those consistent with purpose and need
rubrics_metrics.description: Remind agencies they only need to consider alternatives to a proposed action that are consistent with the purpose of and need for the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid expansive alternatives analysis driven solely by desire to minimize GHGs if alternatives do not meet the project's purpose, which would be inconsistent with NEPA practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid attributing proximate local/regional climate effects to project emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruct agencies not to discuss links between GHG emissions of a proposed action and climate change effects in the vicinity of the proposed action (or worldwide) because any such discussion would be inherently speculative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not treat individual project emissions as proximate causes of local climate impacts; at most disclose emissions but avoid speculative modeling of localized effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on foreseeable direct climate effects, not life-cycle/downstream emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruct agencies to focus on foreseeable climate change effects directly resulting from the proposed action, not 'life-cycle' or 'downstream' emissions, to avoid speculation about remote-in-time or geographically remote effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify that the guidance does not require life-cycle analysis; avoid conflating 'upstream' and 'downstream' discussions in ways that compel speculative analyses of changes likely to occur with or without the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raise de minimis discussion threshold and make it clear
rubrics_metrics.description: EEI recommends raising the 25,000 metric ton/year benchmark to at least 100,000 metric tons/year and removing the 'generally' qualifier so GHGs and climate effects do not need to be discussed below the threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align NEPA discussion threshold with EPA permitting thresholds to avoid reviewing truly de minimis emissions and eliminate ambiguity introduced by 'generally.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify thresholds are not 'significance' indicators for EIS decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that any numerical threshold for discussing GHGs does not in any way indicate 'significance' for deciding whether to prepare an EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reiterate that NEPA’s existing regulatory factors determine significance and that GHG thresholds are only for streamlining discussions, not for triggering EISs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require use of the Federal social cost of carbon metric in NEPA
rubrics_metrics.description: Delete any directive to use the Federal social cost of carbon (SCC) metric to evaluate and monetize costs and benefits in NEPA reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEI argues SCC was developed for regulatory analyses (not project-specific NEPA), has transparency and assumption concerns, and its use would imply proximate causation and require monetization where not appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge courts may require SCC disclosure when agencies monetize benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts have required agencies to disclose the social costs of GHG emissions where they have monetized economic benefits (e.g., royalties, labor income).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance should recognize these judicial decisions and provide a rubric for when monetization/disclosure of social costs may be necessary to produce a legally sufficient NEPA analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission lines are non-emitting; do not treat as direct emission-causing examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmission lines are non-emitting facilities and do not proximately cause changes in generation or emissions in most cases; they should not appear among examples that require programmatic or broad-based GHG NEPA reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using 'constructing transmission towers' as an example of projects that necessarily implicate GHG programmatic review; do not infer generation or emissions changes from construction of transmission absent a clear dedicated new generation connection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on existing information; do not require new climate modeling or extensive data gathering
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not require agencies to engage in climate change modeling or data gathering; at most, rely on existing information to avoid increasing the burden of NEPA analyses disproportionate to the proposed action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current draft is consistent with this approach, but any directive to gather additional data should be limited to cases where cost is reasonable and necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies are not required to adopt mitigation measures in NEPA documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify that agencies are not required to adopt mitigation measures as part of NEPA analyses; NEPA is procedural and mitigation specifications remain within the action agency’s discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While agencies should consider mitigation measures when appropriate, guidance should not suggest NEPA analyses must impose specific mitigation obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply guidance prospectively, not retroactively
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify that the guidance, once final, should apply prospectively and not be applied to ongoing NEPA projects that have already undergone scoping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imposing new requirements on projects mid-process to prevent additional cost, uncertainty, and delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sector-wide assessments to permit qualitative evaluations when precise quantification is difficult
rubrics_metrics.description: Where direct and indirect GHG emissions are difficult to quantify, sector-wide emissions assessments can provide helpful context allowing agencies to provide qualitative assessments of potential impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize that well-substantiated sector-wide analyses (e.g., EIA reports) can inform agency decisions and stakeholder understanding consistent with NEPA’s information-forcing objectives.
